production.note: US model years. KBB's 2021 Ferrari Roma page links model years '2024', '2023' and '2022'; its 2025 address returns the 2024 car (kbb-roma). Evo: 'The Roma coupe was first delivered to customers in 2020 but when the Roma Spider arrived in 2023, Ferrari stopped taking orders for the hard-top car' and 'The Roma has been replaced by the Amalfi' (evo-roma). The Roma Spider is a separate car.

body.note: Front-engined 2+ coupe; the open Roma Spider is sold under its own name.

displacementL.note: 3,855 cc. Ferrari: 'Overall displacement 3855 cc'; Evo panel: '3855cc, twin-turbo' (evo-roma).

drivetrain.note: Front-engined, rear-wheel-drive coupe; inferred from the description (no driven front axle).

transmission.note: Ferrari: '8-speed F1 dual-clutch gearbox'. No manual was offered.

powerHp.note: Ferrari's rating is metric: 620 cv x 0.98632 = 611.5, rounded to 612 hp. Quote (Ferrari technical specifications as rehosted by Auto International): "Max.poweroutput* 456 kW (620 cv) at 5750 - 7500 rpm". ferrari.com also gives '620 cv at 7500 rpm' (ferrari-roma-page). KBB's US listing shows '612 hp' (kbb-roma); Evo prints 611bhp. No separate SAE rating published by Ferrari for the US was found, so powerStandard is DIN PS.

weightLb.note: Ferrari's figure: 1,570 kg x 2.20462 = 3,461.3, rounded to 3,461 lb. Quote (Ferrari technical specifications): "Kerb weight** 1570 kg" (beside "Dry weight** 1472 kg"), footnote "**With optional content". Evo's panel prints the same: "Weight | 1570kg (395bhp/ton)" (evo-roma); KBB's US listing shows '3461 lbs.' (kbb-roma). Coupe with the 8-speed dual-clutch gearbox (the only configuration). Step 3 of the weight order: the manufacturer's kerb weight for a car with optional content (the options are not named; very probably Ferrari's lightweight options), since no standard-car figure was found; a standard car is somewhat heavier.
